chunks: And from him, from Ja'far ibn Muhammad ibn Hakim, from Karram ibn Amr, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), who said:
I said to him, 'A man permits the private part of his concubine to his brother.' He said, 'Yes, there is no objection; he has whatever he has permitted from her.'
ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on a man permitting his brother to have relations with his concubine?
ai.summary: This hadith from the chapter on types of marriage in *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* clarifies the juristic concept of *ibahah* (permission), where a master permits another to share in the sexual rights of his female slave. Imam al-Sadiq (AS) confirms the validity of this arrangement, specifying that the permitted party acquires only the specific rights granted by the owner, reflecting the flexible property rights in Shia fiqh. This ruling underscores the distinction between ownership and usufruct in the context of concubinage during the early Islamic period.
